name: West Java
summary_text: The most concentrated wave of mob violence against transgender women in Indonesia: ten attacks on 45 victim-survivors in Bogor between 30 March and 15 July 2026, documented by Pelangi Nusantara — groups of 10–20 men punched, kicked, threw stones, glass bottles and firecrackers at trans women and stripped some of them naked, filming the assaults for social media under the account @bogorbersihlgbt ('Bogor clean of LGBT'). No alleged perpetrator has been publicly identified, arrested or prosecuted; a trans-rights activist who accompanied women filing police reports said officers 'accepted the case but worked on it half-heartedly,' and some survivors were too afraid to report. Separately, on 22 June 2025 police detained 75 people at a villa raid in the Puncak area of Bogor Regency at a gathering labelled a 'gay party' that violated no law — Amnesty demanded their release. Activists attribute the violence's legitimisation to Perpres 111/2025, which from October 2025 lists 'LGBTQ culture' as a national-resilience threat alongside terrorism and drug abuse: 'people feel able to commit violence arbitrarily because they believe the state has legitimised that violence.' The pattern-plus-impunity combination is West Java-specific; national same-sex criminalisation does not by itself explain the street-vigilante wave with total state inaction and explicit anti-trans branding over four months.

sources.title: Attacks on trans women in Indonesia did not suddenly appear. Here's what's behind them - ABC News
sources.claim_summary: ABC News (15 Aug 2026), drawing on Amnesty International Indonesia and Pelangi Nusantara: groups of 10-20 men attacked and stripped trans women in Bogor in branded videos (@bogorbersihlgbt) after Indonesia's October 2025 presidential regulation listed 'LGBTQ culture' as a national-resilience threat alongside terrorism and drugs; no perpetrator has been identified or prosecuted and police answered ABC with silence; activists link the wave to long-running politicisation of LGBT issues.

sources.title: Indonesian Police Arrest 75 Members of LGBT Community in Puncak Villa - News En.tempo.co
sources.claim_summary: Tempo English (June 2025): Indonesian police detained 75 people at a villa in the Puncak area of Bogor Regency, West Java, after an alleged LGBT gathering — police framed it as a moral offence though no law was violated.

sources.title: Indonesia: Police must release 75 people arrested in discriminatory raid on “gay party” - Amnesty International
sources.claim_summary: Amnesty International (June 2025): demands release of the 75 people detained in the Puncak villa raid, calling it a discriminatory raid on a 'gay party' and noting the gathering violated no law and posed no threat — documenting police mass-detention practice in Bogor, West Java.
